newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET - Parore makes a meal of test warm-up.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET - Parore makes a meal of test warm-up.

text.p: PALMERSTON NORTH, Jan 16 - Test batsman Adam Parore missed out on an excellent chance to get a good look at the England bowling attack on the final morning of the New Zealand Selection 11's cricket match against the tourists on Thursday.
Parore, sure to be named in New Zealand's first-test team tonight, began the day on eight with the Selection 11 on 25 for one wicket, trailing England by 264 runs.
It was an ideal situation for Parore to have a good long innings as a lead-up to the test, starting in Auckland next Friday.
Instead, in the sixth over of the morning, having moved to 13, he pushed forward to fast-medium Chris Silverwood and was well caught by wicketkeeper Alec Stewart low to his right.
Opening batsman Blair Pocock, who started the day on 11, made slow but safe progress through the first hour today.
Matt Horne survived a vehement appeal for a stumping by Stewart off left-arm spinner Phil Tufnell just before the drinks break.
At the break, after 30 overs, the Selection 11 were 55-2, with Pocock on 24 and Horne on eight.
